Entering a new market

How do you get seen in a new market?

Short answer

When an established company enters a new market, it usually brings the message that worked at home. But a new market reads that message differently: buyers know nothing about your reputation, decision-makers build trust in their own way, and competitors already occupy familiar positions. Being seen starts with understanding how this market will read you, then shaping your narrative for it.

Is this you?

  • You’re planning to enter, or have recently entered, the GCC, Australia or another new market
  • Your reputation at home doesn’t seem to travel with you
  • Meetings happen, but decisions don’t follow
  • Your materials are translated, but not really understood
  • Local competitors look and sound more familiar to buyers than you do

Why it happens

A company’s reputation is built over years in one market. In a new market, that history is invisible. What remains is how you present yourself, and that presentation was designed for people who already knew you.

Markets also read the same message differently. What signals confidence in one place can read as distance in another. What sounds premium at home can sound the same as everyone else in a crowded harbour.

How I work on this

  1. Listen: your goals for the market, your strengths at home, and what you already know about the buyers there
  2. Diagnose: how your current positioning and materials are likely to be read by decision-makers in the new market, and where you blend in with competitors
  3. Narrative: a story that carries your strengths into the new market in a way its buyers understand and trust
  4. System: channels, presence, partners and timing for being seen, with execution directed through a specialist network if needed

What you get

  • A clear view of how the new market is likely to see you today
  • A positioning and narrative built for that market’s decision-makers
  • A plan for presence: where to show up, with whom, and in what order
  • Guidance on what to adapt and what to keep from your home-market brand

FAQs

Do you help with licensing, legal set-up or logistics?

No. My work focuses on how you are seen, understood and trusted in the new market: positioning, narrative, presence and the system to deliver them.

When should we start?

Ideally before you enter. A clear diagnosis beforehand usually costs far less than correcting course after the market has formed its first impression.

Which markets do you work with?

Mainly the UAE, the wider GCC and Australia, including companies moving between them.
